title: 388. The psychology of fashion & personal style

sentences.zh: 我是杰玛·斯派克，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》，在这里我们探讨二十岁时最大的改变、时刻和转折，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听又一期节目，当然，我们要在这里剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Anyways, I'm going to give a little heads up to you guys today.
sentences.zh: 总之，今天我要先给大家提个醒。

sentences.en: I'm quite ill.
sentences.zh: 我病得挺重的。

sentences.zh: 如果你在Netflix上观看，你会看到我面前放着这杯茶，这杯茶里其实有个小秘密。

sentences.zh: 里面其实放了三个茶包。

sentences.zh: 我混入了两个柠檬姜茶和一个润喉茶。

sentences.zh: 所以我发明了一种全新的茶口味，而且我现在完全没有味觉。

sentences.en: So it's honestly doing the trick, but throughout this episode, I'm sure you're going to hear some horrible nasal noises, and I'm so sorry, and I wish I could fix it,
sentences.zh: 所以老实说这还挺管用的，但在整期节目中，我确信你们会听到一些难听的鼻音，对此我深表歉意，我真希望能解决它，

sentences.en: but the show must go on, especially because there was no way I was missing...
sentences.zh: 但节目必须继续，尤其是因为我无论如何也不会错过……

sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.zh: 我们刚拿到一些。

sentences.zh: 我绝对不会错过今天的节目，因为这是一期期待已久的节目，可能也是我亲自做过最多研究的节目之一。

sentences.en: We're talking about the psychology of personal style.
sentences.zh: 我们今天聊聊个人风格的心理学。

sentences.en: I have been so drawn into the psychology of fashion recently.
sentences.zh: 我最近深深被时尚心理学所吸引。

sentences.en: I'm not a particularly fashionable person.
sentences.zh: 我并不是一个特别懂时尚的人。

sentences.en: I don't really think about it that often, but just the psychology behind why we wear what we wear, why we choose certain colors, why we are drawn to certain accessories,
sentences.zh: 我其实不常想这些，但对于我们为什么要穿我们穿的衣服、为什么选择特定的颜色、为什么会被特定的配饰吸引，背后的心理学，

sentences.en: even certain animal prints.
sentences.zh: 甚至某些动物纹。

sentences.en: There is a massive rabbit hole that you can fall into looking into this, and I want to share some of my findings.
sentences.zh: 研究这个你会掉进一个巨大的知识深洞，我想分享我的一些发现。

sentences.en: The thing is, what we choose to wear isn't...
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们选择穿什么并不是……

sentences.en: It's not the most important thing about us, and I'm sure there are some people who would disagree with me.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们身上最重要的事情，我确信有些人会不同意我的看法。

sentences.en: There are some diehard fashion fans out there who would say it's the most important thing in the world, but there's definitely plenty of more that matters,
sentences.zh: 外面有一些死忠的时尚迷会说这是世界上最重要的事情，但绝对还有更多更重要的事，

sentences.en: what you do with your time, your values, your hobbies, etc., etc., but when you think about it, getting dressed is incredibly psychologically revealing because it is a ritual.
sentences.zh: 比如你如何利用时间、你的价值观、你的爱好等等，但仔细想想，穿衣打扮在心理上具有极其深刻的揭示性，因为它是一种仪式。

sentences.en: It is a thing that we do every single day, and what we choose to get dressed in every single day, that decision can reveal some really significant things
sentences.zh: 这是我们每天都在做的事情，我们每天选择穿什么衣服，这个决定可以揭示一些非常重大的事情，

sentences.en: about our personality, about our insecurities, how we were in childhood.
sentences.zh: 关于我们的性格，关于我们的不安全感，以及我们童年时的经历。

sentences.en: It's honestly so mind-blowing what we're going to get into today.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我们今天要探讨的内容简直让人大开眼界。

sentences.en: Whether you care about fashion a lot, you have a Vogue subscription, whether you care about it a medium amount or not at all,
sentences.zh: 无论你非常关心时尚，订阅了《Vogue》，还是对时尚半懂不懂，或者完全不关心，

sentences.en: I really don't care.
sentences.zh: 我其实并不在乎。

sentences.en: Because you're going to hear a fact today that is going to blow your mind.
sentences.zh: 因为你今天会听到一个让你大跌眼镜的事实。

sentences.en: I promise you that.
sentences.zh: 我向你保证。

sentences.en: And you may also learn how to make better style choices based on your identity and your personality.
sentences.zh: 并且你还可能会根据你的身份和性格，学到如何做出更好的风格选择。

sentences.en: And you may also save yourself some money and some time by being able to curate a wardrobe based on what you're going to find out about yourself today.
sentences.zh: 通过根据你今天对自己的了解来精心打造衣橱，你还可以省下一些钱和时间。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the psychology of personal style.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们进入个人风格的心理学。

sentences.en: I think the magical thing about fashion and personal style is that clothing is obviously one of the most immediate and obvious forms of self-expression that we can have.
sentences.zh: 我认为时尚和个人风格最神奇的地方在于，服装显然是我们所能拥有的最直接、最明显自我表达形式之一。

sentences.en: And that is what makes it so mentally significant because it's basically looking at what somebody wears every day can help us decipher so much about how they want us to see them.
sentences.zh: 这就是它在心理上如此重大的原因，因为观察某人每天穿什么基本上可以帮我们解读出很多关于他们希望我们如何看待他们的信息。

sentences.en: Your clothes aren't just pieces of fabric.
sentences.zh: 你的衣服不仅仅是布料。

sentences.en: They are a first impression.
sentences.zh: 它们是第一印象。

sentences.en: They are a profession for some people.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，它们是一种职业。

sentences.en: They are an identity hallmark.
sentences.zh: 它们是身份的标志。

sentences.en: And they cause a reaction in other people.
sentences.zh: 它们会引起其他人的反应。

sentences.en: A 2023 Canadian study found that people immediately make some pretty rapid and pretty on-the-nose conclusions about everything from our cognitive state
sentences.zh: 2023年的一项加拿大研究发现，人们在看到我们穿的衣服几秒钟内，就会对我们的方方面面迅速做出相当直接且切中要害的结论，

sentences.en: to our social status to our aesthetic status within seconds of seeing what we're wearing.
sentences.zh: 从我们的认知状态到我们的社会地位，再到我们的审美地位。

sentences.en: And they're very accurate assessments.
sentences.zh: 而且这些评估非常准确。

sentences.en: And as people, we know that.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们深知这一点。

sentences.en: We know that whether we like it or not, people are making broader assessments about us based on our clothes.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，无论我们喜欢与否，人们都在根据我们的衣服对我们做出更广泛的评估。

sentences.en: It's why we agonize over a first date dress or we agonize over what to wear to a job interview or what color of jeans is best when they all kind of look the same.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们会为第一次约会的裙子而纠结，或者为面试穿什么、或者当牛仔裤看起来都差不多时哪种颜色最好而纠结。

sentences.en: Those reactions we get to our clothes are part of what actually informs our personal style from a very, very young age.
sentences.zh: 我们对衣服所得到的那些反应，正是从非常非常小的时候开始实际塑造我们个人风格的一部分。

sentences.en: I think we take personal style for granted sometimes and we think that it's just kind of like appeared or it's just based on trends.
sentences.zh: 我认为有时我们把个人风格视为理所当然，觉得它只是凭空出现，或者只是基于潮流。

sentences.en: But from very early on, we are actually conditioned to choose the kinds of clothes that we continue to wear for the rest of our lives.
sentences.zh: 但从很早开始，我们实际上就已经被塑造去选择那些我们将伴随一生并继续穿着的衣服。

sentences.en: And I think that is something not many of us know.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这是我们许多人所不知道的。

sentences.en: Our childhood is a huge fundamental part of our fashion choices.
sentences.zh: 我们的童年是我们时尚选择的一个巨大的基础部分。

sentences.en: And this is because of a very fundamental psychological process called associative learning.
sentences.zh: 这是因为一个非常基础的心理学过程，叫做联想学习。

sentences.en: Essentially, at some stage, your brain begins to link clothing choices with certain feelings and certain outcomes that were either good, bad, neutral, exciting, terrible,
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，在某个阶段，你的大脑开始将服装选择与某些感觉以及某些结果联系起来，这些结果可能是好的、坏的、中性的、兴奋的、糟糕的，

sentences.en: or something else.
sentences.zh: 或者是别的什么。

sentences.en: So this starts actually fairly randomly.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是从相当随机的事情开始的。

sentences.en: Most associative learning does.
sentences.zh: 大多数联想学习都是如此。

sentences.en: But obviously, when we're young, when we're kids, like we don't pick our clothes.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，当我们还小的时候，当我们是孩子的时候，我们不会自己挑选衣服。

sentences.en: Our parents pick our clothes for us.
sentences.zh: 我们的父母替我们挑选衣服。

sentences.en: And their style is essentially our style.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的风格基本上就是我们的风格。

sentences.en: My mom was born in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈出生在威斯康星州。

sentences.en: My dad was born in Queensland.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸出生在昆士兰州。

sentences.en: And so when I was a kid, I was always dressed in like a mix of
sentences.zh: 所以当我还是个孩子的时候，我总是穿着混合了

sentences.en: Oshkosh-Bagosh overalls, if you know what those are, and like beachwear and t-shirts.
sentences.zh: 奥什科什背带裤（如果你知道那是什么的话），还有海滩装和T恤。

sentences.en: You know, you don't really have a choice.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你其实别无选择。

sentences.en: But what you do start to realize and notice is when certain items get a positive reaction and when certain items don't or how certain items make you feel.
sentences.zh: 但你开始意识到并注意到的是，什么时候某些单品会得到积极的反应，什么时候不会，或者某些单品会给你带来什么样的感受。

sentences.en: What made you feel comfortable?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你感到舒适？

sentences.en: What made you feel safe?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你感到安全？

sentences.en: What made you feel close to your parents?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你感到与父母亲近？

sentences.en: What made you fit in?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你觉得合群呢？

sentences.en: I remember there was this certain long dress I used to wear that my grandma bought me.
sentences.zh: 我记得我以前常穿一件我奶奶给我买的长裙。

sentences.en: And the first time I wore it, like everybody in my family made such a huge fuss about how nice I looked in it.
sentences.zh: 而且我第一次穿它的时候，家里每个人都夸我穿得特别好看，小题大做地惊叹了一番。

sentences.en: And I would wear it all the time.
sentences.zh: 然后我就会一直穿它。

sentences.en: I would literally twirl in it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至会在里面转圈圈。

sentences.en: I would go up to strangers to show them my great dress and they'd be like, where the hell is this child's parents?
sentences.zh: 我会跑到陌生人面前展示我那件漂亮的裙子，他们大概会想：这小孩的爸妈到底上哪儿去了？

sentences.en: But that was such a learned association and it was so funny.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种习得的联结，而且非常搞笑。

sentences.en: Last week I was looking for an outfit for a friend's wedding and I found a dress that looks really similar and it was like this gravitational pull.
sentences.zh: 上周我在为朋友的婚礼找衣服时，找到了一件看起来真的很相似的裙子，就好像有一种引力一样。

sentences.en: Like this is something that I know.
sentences.zh: 就像这是我熟悉的东西。

sentences.en: This is something that like, I have this long ago positive association with and I ended up buying the dress for that reason alone.
sentences.zh: 这是我很久以前就对其抱有积极联结的东西，最终我仅仅因为这个原因买下了这条裙子。

sentences.en: I also remember feeling the most myself in like my Buzz Lightyear shirt.
sentences.zh: 我也记得穿着巴斯光年的衬衫时，最能做自己。

sentences.en: I knew that was comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我知道那是舒服的。

sentences.en: I knew I could move around.
sentences.zh: 我知道我可以活动自如。

sentences.en: I knew I could be a child in that.
sentences.zh: 我知道我在那里面可以像个孩子。

sentences.en: That was my safety blanket.
sentences.zh: 那是我的安全毯。

sentences.en: So that's how you learn.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你学习的方式。

sentences.en: But on the other side, you also learn, yes, through positive things, also through negative things.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，你也会学到东西，是的，通过积极的事情，也通过消极的事情。

sentences.en: You learn what gets you teased, what elicits negative reactions.
sentences.zh: 你会知道什么会招致嘲笑，什么会引起消极的反应。

sentences.en: Maybe it was wearing a crop top in your childhood and you were teased for it.
sentences.zh: 也许你在童年时穿过露脐装，因此遭到过嘲笑。

sentences.en: You were shamed for it.
sentences.zh: 你为此感到羞耻。

sentences.en: Some kids said terrible things for you and so you grow up thinking you can't wear that and you never do or you wear a type of pant or a type of jean that ripped or gave you a rash
sentences.zh: 有些孩子对你说过难听的话，所以你长大后觉得你不能穿那个，并且永远都不会穿，或者你穿了一种会撕裂或让你起红疹的裤子或牛仔裤

sentences.en: and for some reason you've avoided that for the rest of your life.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，你在余生中都在避开它。

sentences.en: Clothes carry learnt associations.
sentences.zh: 衣服承载着习得的联结。

sentences.en: That is why certain clothes, like we were talking about, feel emotionally relevant because they are often tied to memories, memories, the same memories
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么某些衣服，正如我们刚才讨论的那样，会让人在情感上觉得有关联，因为它们通常与记忆捆绑在一起，记忆，即那些与我们身份建构息息相关的相同记忆

sentences.en: that our identity is built on.
sentences.zh: 我们的身份正是建立在这些记忆之上的。

sentences.en: In fact, researchers from the University of College London looked at this in great detail and they basically said in this article they wrote, and I can't remember the name of it,
sentences.zh: 事实上，伦敦大学学院的研究人员对此进行了非常详细的研究，他们基本上在他们写的一篇文章中提到过，虽然我记不得名字了

sentences.en: but they said that clothes are instruments for anchoring the self and remembering the past and through that they enhance our well-being.
sentences.zh: 但他们说，衣服是锚定自我和铭记过去的工具，并通过这种方式提升我们的幸福感。

sentences.en: They are like this weird rope that ties together who we want to be, who we are now, and who we were in the past in like one long line.
sentences.zh: 它们就像一根奇异的绳索，把我们想成为的人、现在的我们以及过去的我们串联成一条长长的线。

sentences.en: Clothes are a mix of, yes, practicality and what's affordable, but also of mood and memory and that is constantly playing subconsciously in the background of
sentences.zh: 衣服既是实用性和可负担性的结合，也是情绪和记忆的结合，这些东西一直在潜意识里不断发挥作用

sentences.en: the choices you make around fashion every single day.
sentences.zh: 潜移默化地影响着你每天做出的时尚选择。

sentences.en: It's incredibly emotionally evocative.
sentences.zh: 它在情感上极其能够唤起共鸣。

sentences.en: It's incredibly representative of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 它极具对过去的代表性。

sentences.en: It's why I think we struggle to throw out items that we don't wear anymore but used to be our favorites.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为我们很难扔掉那些不再穿了、但曾经是我们的最爱的东西。

sentences.en: It's why we have really distinct childhood memories, not just of moments, but of the clothes that we wore in them.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我们有非常鲜明的童年记忆，不仅仅是关于某个时刻的，还包括我们当时穿的衣服。

sentences.en: They are not neutral iteMs.
sentences.zh: 它们可不是中立的物品。

sentences.en: Beyond these past memories, research also shows that your baseline personality can also predict how you will dress, essentially there is this kind of theory that if you were to
sentences.zh: 除了这些过去的记忆，研究还表明，你的基准个性也可以预测你的穿着方式，基本上有这样一种理论，如果你去

sentences.en: take somebody's outfit you could pick it apart and basically make a composite of what their personality is like based on some some pretty amazing correlations
sentences.zh: 拿走某人的服装，你可以将其拆解，并根据性格属性和服装选择之间一些相当惊人的相关性

sentences.en: between personality attributes and clothing choices.
sentences.zh: 基本上拼凑出他们的性格是怎样的。

sentences.en: We can specifically look at this through the big five
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过大五人格

sentences.en: personality domains or personality principles.
sentences.zh: 人格领域或人格原则来具体看待这一点。

sentences.en: So just as a little refresh, the biggest theory on personality is that our personality is made of five traits.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个小复习，关于人格的最大理论是我们的性格由五个特质组成。

sentences.en: Those are extroversion, openness to experience,
sentences.zh: 它们是外向性、开放性、

sentences.en: neuroticism, agreeableness, and conscientiousness.
sentences.zh: 神经质、宜人性和责任心。

sentences.en: And if we look at the profile of each of these, where you sit on those ladder, where you sit on that spectrum for each of those traits is going to essentially reveal
sentences.zh: 如果我们看一下其中每一个的档案，你在那些阶梯上所处的位置，你在每一个这些特质的频谱上所处的位置，基本上就会揭示

sentences.en: your clothing choices.
sentences.zh: 你的服装选择。

sentences.en: So starting with openness to experience, people high in this trait often value play and they value aesthetics and they are creative and they are curious and inquisitive
sentences.zh: 从对经验的开放性开始，在这个特质上得分高的人通常重视玩乐，他们重视美学，他们具有创造力、好奇心、求知欲

sentences.en: and unconventional.
sentences.zh: 以及不拘一格。

sentences.en: Because of that, according to a paper published in the Polish Psychological Forum in 2024, if you are high in that, you are more likely to seek original items of clothing.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，根据2024年发表在《波兰心理学论坛》上的一篇论文，如果你在这方面很高，你更有可能寻找原创的服装。

sentences.en: You are typically more fashionable as they called it.
sentences.zh: 用他们的话说，你通常更具时尚感。

sentences.en: You are most likely to be somebody who adopts the new trend first because of that intellectual curiosity and that kind of experimental personality that you have.
sentences.zh: 由于你的这种求知欲和那种实验性的个性，你极有可能是最先采用新潮流的人。

sentences.en: People, in contrast, who are low in openness to experience,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，那些对经验开放性较低的人，

sentences.en: there's actually been all this research that they wear more subdued clothes.
sentences.zh: 事实上已经有很多研究表明他们穿的衣服更加素雅。

sentences.en: They're more likely to want a capsule wardrobe.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能想要一个胶囊衣橱。

sentences.en: They're more likely to gravitate towards the same shapes, colors, like, yeah, silhouettes or features of clothing that they have for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能倾向于选择他们长期以来一直穿着的相同的版型、颜色、比如，是的，剪影或服装特征。

sentences.en: So openness to experience is this first thing that we can kind of divide fashion profiles by.
